scenario.prompt_to_agent:
After a config-cleanup window, a user on pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) reports they
lost all reach across the fabric -- pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) is unreachable,
though pc_0_1 can still ping its own gateway 10.0.1.1. Both spine
routers report their BGP session toward leaf_router_0_1 down at the
same time, yet leaf_router_0_1's uplink interfaces show UP and its FRR
daemons are all running. Investigate.

injection.action: delete both spine neighbor statements from the running BGP config

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: leaf_router_0_1 BGP neighbor configuration
Mechanism: leaf_router_0_1 (AS 65201) normally peers with
  spine_router_0_0 (neighbor 172.16.0.6 remote-as 65100) and
  spine_router_0_1 (neighbor 172.16.0.10 remote-as 65101). Both
  neighbor statements were deleted from the running config, so bgpd
  sends a Cease notification and drops both sessions. With zero peers
  the leaf stops advertising 10.0.1.0/24 (the spines withdraw it
  immediately) and stops learning 10.0.0.0/24, so pc_0_1 is isolated
  even though bgpd is running and every link is UP.
Localization: leaf_router_0_1
Root cause: both BGP neighbor statements removed under
  `router bgp 65201` on leaf_router_0_1
Fix: re-add the two neighbor statements on leaf_router_0_1 (see [FIX]).
scenario.fix_spec:
Re-add the spine neighbors on leaf_router_0_1:
`vtysh -c "configure terminal" -c "router bgp 65201"
 -c "neighbor 172.16.0.6 remote-as 65100"
 -c "neighbor 172.16.0.10 remote-as 65101"`
Note: the injection changed only the running config; the intended
config is still intact in /etc/frr/frr.conf, so `service frr restart`
on leaf_router_0_1 is an equally correct fix (it reloads the file and
re-creates both neighbors).
scoring_axes: must-identify-component: BGP neighbor configuration removed / no configured peers
must-distinguish-symptom-pattern: uplink interfaces UP and bgpd running while both spine sessions are down -- a config fault, not a link or daemon fault
bonus-cites-missing-neighbors: names the missing neighbor statements (172.16.0.6 / spine_router_0_0 and 172.16.0.10 / spine_router_0_1) or shows `show bgp summary` with zero peers

agent.diagnosis_text:
Affected component: FRR BGP configuration on leaf_router_0_1 (bgpd process/neighbors). Mechanism: With no eBGP peering to the spines, leaf_router_0_1 learns no fabric routes (e.g., 10.0.0.0/24), so it generates ICMP Destination Net Unreachable for traffic from its access VLAN. From pc_0_1, pings to 10.0.0.2 fail with “From 10.0.1.1 Destination Net Unreachable,” proving the leaf lacks a route beyond its local subnet. Localization: On leaf_router_0_1, both uplinks are up and correctly addressed (eth0 172.16.0.7/31, eth1 172.16.0.11/31). bgpd is listening (tcp/179 present in netstat). However, vtysh shows “% No BGP neighbors found,” and the running config contains no neighbor statements under router bgp 65201—only “network 10.0.1.0/24”. On both spines, “show bgp summary” lists neighbors 172.16.0.7 and 172.16.0.11 in Active, confirming the leaf isn’t establishing sessions. Root cause: The config-cleanup removed the BGP neighbor stanzas on leaf_router_0_1, leaving bgpd running but with no peers. Corrective fix: Re-add neighbors on leaf_router_0_1 to both spines, e.g.:
router bgp 65201
 neighbor 172.16.0.6 remote-as 65100
 neighbor 172.16.0.10 remote-as 65101
 address-family ipv4 unicast
  network 10.0.1.0/24
 exit-address-family
Then write/commit the integrated config and verify “show bgp summary” reaches Established on both sessions. This will restore reachability to 10.0.0.0/24 across the fabric.

Correct remediation: re-add the two spine BGP neighbors (or restart FRR to reload config) and verify sessions reach Established, which matches the expected fix.

Investigation log shows the leaf has no BGP neighbors (% No BGP neighbors found), BGP port is listening, pings from pc_0_1 fail with ICMP Destination Net Unreachable (leaf acting as gateway), and spines show neighbor entries in Active — together these observations support the diagnosis that neighbor statements were removed on leaf_router_0_1 causing loss of fabric routes. Minor inconsistency (systemd shows frr inactive) is present but does not contradict the core evidence.
